channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

Nature Communications: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
item.description: Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse structural ensembles. We present IDPForge that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP and IDR ensembles that maintain folded domains with options to conform to experimental data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
item.description: Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
item.description: The Arg/N-degron pathway plays a central role in plant development, germination, and submersion tolerance. Here, the authors show that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1, demonstrate an off-switch for calmodulin-controlled ubiquitination, and engineer nanobodies that can redirect PRT1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
item.description: Spirochetes twist through tissues with a powerful corkscrew motion driven by curved internal flagella. Here, authors use cryo-EM to show that an asymmetric protein sheath on a conserved flagellin core shapes these flagella, setting the filament curvature needed for motility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sequence Display generates large-scale sequence–activity datasets for reprogramming SlugCas9 toward difficult-to-access PAMs
item.description: Compact CRISPR-Cas9 enzymes are easier to deliver but recognize few targets. Here, authors use Sequence Display to generate large-scale SlugCas9 sequence–activity datasets and apply protein language models to engineer variants that recognize difficult NNAN PAMs and edit selected human genomic sites.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lamprey and hagfish VLRB signalling complex VLRB-GPIbβ-GPIX originates from lymphocyte-specific duplication of a platelet adhesion module
item.description: The jawless vertebrate antigen receptor VLRB functions analogously to the B cell receptor, despite bearing no structural similarity to it. Here the authors identify the signalling complex downstream of VLRB and show that the origin of the genes encoding the signalosome is an ancient platelet unit that has been duplicated in the lymphocyte lineage.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
item.description: Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
item.description: The molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are not fully resolved. Here the authors assess the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins.

item.title: Nature Communications: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
item.description: Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

item.title: Nature Communications: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
item.description: The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently.

item.title: Nature Communications: Npl4 decodes polyubiquitin length and undergoes D1-gated exchange on p97/VCP
item.description: p97 maintains protein quality by processing ubiquitin-tagged proteins. This report shows how Npl4 reads ubiquitin-chain length and how p97 ATPase activity controls Npl4 exchange, which is altered by disease-linked variants

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
item.description: In this study, the authors map how SARS-CoV-2 proteins NSP8, NSP12 and N interact with viral RNA during infection, revealing regulatory sites that control viral replication and translation, and offering potential targets for antiviral strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
item.description: The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
item.description: Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’).

item.title: Nature Communications: Real-time quantification of skeletal muscle metabolism in healthy men using hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate reveals training-dependent adaptation
item.description: This study combines hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure human muscle metabolism in real time, revealing training-dependent metabolic adaptations and linking ¹³C metabolite ratios to established measures of muscle energetics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host diet may shape bat RNA viromes within geographic and phylogenetic constraints at a global-scale
item.description: By analyzing 1,627 bat RNA viromes from 78 species worldwide, the study shows that geography and host evolution shape bat viral communities more strongly than diet, while feeding ecology plays a secondary role in viral exposure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogeny and intraspecific variability dominate nitrogen fixer biomass responses to nitrogen enrichment
item.description: Nitrogen enrichment alters the growth of nitrogen-fixing plants, but responses vary widely. This meta-analysis shows that phylogeny and intraspecific variation are major contributors to that variability.

item.title: Nature Communications: Equipositioning of chromosomes in the polyploid archaeon Haloferax volcanii by HpaAB
item.description: How the archaeon Haloferax volcanii segregates its multi-copy chromosomes during cell division is unclear. Here, the authors identify two proteins required for an equidistant positioning mechanism, maintaining uniform spacing between chromosomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enzymes can activate and mobilize dense biomolecular condensates across scales
item.description: Enzymes operate in highly crowded cellular environments, yet the impact of crowding on their function remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that enzyme activity increases molecular mobility in crowded protein droplets, suggesting a feedback mechanism between catalysis and the physical properties of the surrounding environment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
item.description: The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
item.description: In this study, Yang et al showed that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families in haploid spermatids. Their study revealed a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin (PMSC) critical for male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
item.description: Early detection of scoliosis is critical for timely intervention, but current screening lacks accuracy. Here the authors develop a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for accurate, intelligent scoliosis identification.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
item.description: Poxviruses transcribe mRNA inside a sealed core, but how it escapes was unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and integrative modelling, the authors resolve a pore in the core wall, built from three viral proteins, that may release the mRNA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
item.description: Chemical imaging can reveal cellular structures without labels, but capturing their rapid 3D dynamics remains challenging. Here, the authors develop mid-infrared photothermal microscopy for video-rate 3D chemical imaging, revealing diverse lipid droplet movements in living cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
item.description: Golparian et al. designed and validated (13,701 global gonococcal genomes) SensiTyper, a rule-based framework predicting antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and susceptibility-guided individualized gonorrhoea treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Canopy nutrient balance predicts autumn senescence across U.S. forests
item.description: Canopy nutrient balance helps sustain leaf activity through the growing season. The study finds that higher canopy N:P is linked to earlier autumn senescence, whereas higher N:K is linked to later senescence across U.S. forests.

item.title: Nature Communications: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
item.description: In this study, the authors use nationwide genomic data collected across sectors in Japan to identify closely related antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Campylobacter isolates in food and humans, highlighting the value of integrated One Health surveillance.

item.title: Nature Communications: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
item.description: B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Programmable hydrogel-nanocapsule protein delivery system targeting dense cartilage regeneration for osteoarthritis therapy
item.description: In osteoarthritis, protein therapeutics show poor joint retention and cartilage penetration. Here, authors develop a programmable two-stage, enzyme-responsive hydrogel-nanocapsule system to deliver a model protein drug and promote cartilage regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
item.description: Down syndrome is a complex condition which results in immune alterations, including higher risk of autoimmune diseases. Here the authors show by single cell and spatial transcriptomics that the differentiation of thymic T cell precursors is disturbed in Down syndrome, which might underpin the functional alterations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
item.description: The pathogen Listeria monocytogenes recruits host proteins to its surface within infected cells for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Here, Woida et al. adapt the split-TurboID technique to identify such proteins and show how a secreted effector co-opts a host deubiquitinase to counteract host restriction of bacterial spread.

item.title: Nature Communications: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
item.description: Functional characterization of the bacterial cell wall remodeling hydrolase LytU with distinct enzymatic activity in Staphylococcus aureus contributing to vancomycin resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
item.description: By comparing testis cell development across four mammals, this study shows that tree shrews more closely resemble primates than mice in key stages of sperm formation, supporting their use as a complementary model of human male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
item.description: In this study, the authors show that thermal stress impacts the microbiome of the sea anemone Exaiptasia diaphana differentially. Chronic and acute stress strongly affects the more sensitive line’s microbiome while the temperature tolerant line’s microbiome changed over time but not with temperature exposure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Darutigenol ameliorates experimental colitis via promoting Akkermansia muciniphila -mediated proline synthesis
item.description: Here, the authors show that Darutigenol inhibits host IDO1 expression to drive A. muciniphila expansion and proline synthesis, thereby alleviating inflammation and presenting a potential strategy for IBD treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
item.description: This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet (X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
item.description: Here, they determine that tet (X4)-carrying Salmonella remains rare in China but is being detected more often and in a wider range of bacterial sequence types and plasmids, supporting continued surveillance.

item.title: Nature Communications: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
item.description: Conway et al. utilize recent advances in cellular cryo-electron tomography to image the human mitotic spindle at nanometer resolution and reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
item.description: Some plant RNA viruses use 3′ tRNA-like structures to promote translation without poly(A) tails. Here, the authors reveal how the tobacco mosaic virus tRNA-like structure directly engages host ribosomes to facilitate translation initiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
item.description: Poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) are key regulators of mRNA stability. Star-PAP stabilizes insulin receptor mRNA to maintain adipose health and its loss causes lipodystrophy and insulin resistance, while pyruvate rescues the defects, highlighting RNA polyadenylation as a key to adipose homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Local albumin excess exacerbates Candida albicans -induced inflammasome activation linked with hyperinflammation during vulvovaginal candidiasis
item.description: This study shows that high vaginal albumin in vulvovaginal candidiasis is not merely a correlate of inflammation, but can drive dysfunctional hyperinflammation by promoting fungal induced inflammasome activation, while compromising fungal clearance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
item.description: Nishinami et al. show that peptides from the sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, condense bacterial ribosomes and inhibit protein synthesis, revealing a biophysical antimicrobial strategy targeting intracellular organization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
item.description: Resistance selection in wastewater is poorly understood. In this study, the authors show that E. coli are selected for in Swedish hospital sewers, but not in municipal treatment plants and identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as drivers that enable targeted measures to manage risks for resistance evolution.

Nature Communications: Long-read sequencing reveals telomere inheritance patterns from human trios
item.description: Using long-read sequencing of 75 family trios, the authors show telomere length is heritable and varies by chromosome arm, with paternally inherited telomeres often longer than maternal ones, offering insight into aging and disease risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
item.description: Altered lipid metabolism is linked to cancer progression. Here, authors show that loss of sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 accelerates leukemia growth by modulating sphingolipid metabolism and potentiating MAPK signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM reveals major proteolysis independent substrate rearrangements in a complement C5 convertase surrogate complex(es)
item.description: The authors use electron microscopy to capture 6 different states of complement C5 bound to and induced by an inactive surrogate convertase. This conformational activation of C5 is shown to be sufficient for lysis of red blood cells in serum.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells
item.description: Chromatin accessibility QTLs can reveal how genetic variants influence gene regulation, but the role of nucleosome organisation remains unclear. Here, the authors map genetic effects on nucleosome‑free regions and positioned nucleosomes in human skeletal muscle, linking regulatory variants to chromatin architecture and disease-associated traits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
item.description: Here, using deep mutational scanning, the authors show that the Zika virus protein NS5 is constrained by competing demands for viral replication and immune evasion, and identify mutations that selectively disrupt interferon antagonism while maintaining viral replication, resulting in an attenuated virus in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
item.description: The authors develop CPRISP, an interpretable AI framework that predicts interactions between circular RNAs and RNA-binding proteins, reveals conserved binding patterns, and prioritizes candidate compounds for neurodegenerative diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
item.description: Brain-wide association studies link brain structure to mental health, but the underlying genetics remain unclear. Here, the authors integrate brain- and genome-wide analyses to identify two brain-mental health modes with distinct genetic architectures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lipidated macrocyclic peptide S-880008 inhibits SARS-CoV-2 fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation at conserved spike sites
item.description: S-880008 is a lipidated macrocyclic peptide that broadly inhibits SARS-CoV-2 variants. By locking spike proteins in a fusion-incompetent state through interactions with conserved sites, it blocks viral entry and protects against infection in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
item.description: The Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago transformed Earth’s atmosphere and forced early life to adapt. This study shows that proteins across the tree of life became progressively more oxidized over this period, consistent with evolution favouring lower-energy sequences.

item.title: Nature Communications: Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation
item.description: Although serine restriction has been proposed as a strategy to limit tumor growth, its therapeutic utility remains uncertain and may compromise anti-tumor immunity. Here, the authors show that serine enhances CD8⁺ T cell function and that serine supplementation may help overcome resistance to PD-1 blockade.

item.title: Nature Communications: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
item.description: Thrombin, an enzyme involved in inflammation, modifies α-synuclein by removing six amino acids. This subtle modification affects its structure and aggregation, suggesting a link between inflammation and processes involved in Parkinson’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
item.description: In this study, the authors use longitudinal metagenomics profiling to show that cattle upper respiratory viromes display age-dependent succession and phage-linked bacterial adaptation during early life, and harbor bovine-derived coronavirus and adenovirus genomes reflecting cross-host evolutionary signatures.

item.title: Nature Communications: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
item.description: This study presents a tailored erythropoietin fused to engineered albumin for extended plasma half-life after intravenous and subcutaneous delivery in mice. Following invasive or intranasal delivery, it promotes sustained erythrocyte proliferation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
item.description: DNA polymerase η helps cells copy damaged DNA, but its role in unperturbed replication is unclear. Here, the authors map its activity in human cells and show that it preferentially copies the lagging DNA strand and regions replicated late, linking its use to mutation patterns in cancer genomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
item.description: Root microbiomes shape terrestrial ecosystems, yet identifying keystone microbes remains difficult. By statistically inferring assembly rules, the authors reveal endophytic fungi as hidden drivers reorganizing below-ground symbioses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Impression-R1 for radiological impression generation with multicenter benchmarking and prospective evaluations
item.description: Authors develop a domain-specific large reasoning model for radiological impression generation called Impression-R1. It generates diagnostic summaries from radiology findings and performed favorably across institutions and public datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
item.description: A one-time gene therapy targeting MSH3 reduced the expansion of HD-causing DNA repeats in preclinical studies. Patient-based modeling predicts this approach could delay symptom onset by years and meaningfully slow Huntington’s disease progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
item.description: CADS brings together 22,022 diverse CT scans with annotations of 167 structures across the body. The openly available dataset and AI model enable large-scale whole-body anatomical analysis and perform robustly across public and hospital data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
item.description: A study in Finnish and UK adults finds that deaths during extreme heat and cold are substantially higher among people with both pre-existing disease and socioeconomic disadvantage, identifying them as a priority for climate adaptation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
item.description: The study reveals how a herpesvirus protein complex changes shape to help the virus enter cells. A conserved molecular switch may offer a target for treatments against multiple herpesviruses.

item.title: Nature Communications: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
item.description: Here, the authors introduce scBOA, a Bayesian optimization tool that helps researchers choose single-cell analysis settings for cell-type annotation. They perform benchmarking to show that performance depends on the dataset, reference and objective.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1–NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice
item.description: The role of hippocampal perineuronal nets in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, authors show that vCA1 nets regulate morphine CPP acquisition via PV-IN-mediated inhibition and glutamatergic output to NAcC D1-MSNs.

item.title: Nature Communications: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
item.description: In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
item.description: The impact of sex-based differences on clinical outcomes of antibody-drug conjugates in patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) remains unclear. In here, the authors show that male patients have higher Nectin cell adhesion molecule 4 (NECTIN-4) expression as well as longer median overall survival and time on treatment while female patients experience higher rates of primary resistant disease despite similar baseline characteristics.

item.title: Nature Communications: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
item.description: Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
item.description: Researchers show that vaccine-induced antibodies targeting a surface sugar of Klebsiella pneumoniae can kill many clinically important strains, supporting simpler vaccine designs that may help combat neonatal sepsis and antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
item.description: RNA-binding proteins are thought to enhance transcription by forming condensates. Here, the authors show that nascent RNA recruits FUS to boost polymerase loading and accelerate elongation by preventing R-loops, without requiring macroscopic condensates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
item.description: The locus coeruleus, the brain’s main source of noradrenaline, helps regulate stress responses. Here, authors show that dynorphin co-released from lateral hypothalamus neurons acts as an anxiolytic brake in the locus coeruleus, balancing excitatory signals to control stress-induced anxiety in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
item.description: Nanoparticles functionalized with a majority of positively and a minority of negatively charged ligands can selectively trigger cancer cell death. Here, the authors explore the effect of modulating the minority, negative, ligands and report changes in intracellular localization patterns with different ligands.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
item.description: The intestine remembers past injury. Arozamena and colleagues reveal that transcriptional and epigenetic memory accelerates future repair, with IFN-gamma encoding inflammatory memory and dedifferentiation leaving a distinct regenerative imprint.

item.title: Nature Communications: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
item.description: Light influences how fishes sense their environment, but tracking the history of visual adaptations has been difficult. This study finds that melanosomes in modern and fossil fishes provide insights into early vertebrate sensory evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
item.description: Dengue is surging in temperate southern Brazil. This study links the rise to the spread and increasing infestation levels of Aedes aegypti, rather than to shifts in climate suitability, and shows that viral lineages persist locally for years.

item.title: Nature Communications: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
item.description: HIV persists during antiretroviral therapy in reservoirs that rapidly drive viral rebound when treatment stops. The authors here show that chimeric antigen receptor-engineered NK cells delay viral rebound and restrict rebound-associated viral lineages, leaving proviruses in less active chromatin.

item.title: Nature Communications: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
item.description: Biological evolution is often thought of as unrepeatable, dependent upon myriad historical contingencies. Contrary to this view, this study shows detailed similarities in the ways that vertebrate species adapt to aquatic, terrestrial and aerial environments despite being separated by millions of years of evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
item.description: Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
item.description: Fossil dinosaur eggs are extremely rare, and there is uncertainty about their ancestral anatomy and evolution. A newly described Early Jurassic sauropodomorph soft-shelled egg offers valuable insights into the reproductive biology of dinosaurs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
item.description: The clearance of apoptotic cells, or efferocytosis, reprograms macrophages towards a pro-resolving phenotype to facilitate tissue repair. Here, the authors identify IKKβ as an upstream regulator of immunoregulatory and reparative processes, showing that MerTK activation by apoptotic cells transiently activates an IKKβ-dependent NFKB/p38 axis, inducing IL-10 production, Rac1-mediated continuing efferocytosis, and activation of a Myc–TET2–PD-L1 pathway that promotes regulatory T cell expansion.

item.title: Nature Communications: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
item.description: Metagenomic tools underestimate linear viral genome completeness due to circularity bias. In this study, the authors track within-species genomic termini conservation across metagenomic datasets to recover and validate 1,585 complete linear viral genomes, revealing a 21-fold expansion of hidden RNA and DNA viruses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
item.description: The clinical applicability and generalizability of foundation models (FM) that use self-supervised pre-training in comparison to task- specific (TS) models that utilize end-to-end learning remains to be elucidated. Here, the authors show that while FMs demonstrate better utility in data-scarce scenarios, they still require considerable task-specific training to match TS diagnostic and grading performance and consume more energy than smaller TS models.

item.title: Nature Communications: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
item.description: This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
item.description: The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
item.description: This study presents AbOptimizer, a computational framework that edits antibody sequences to improve multiple therapeutic properties. Tests on three antibodies show improved affinity, specificity and stability-related profiles.

item.title: Nature Communications: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
item.description: Vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching drives atherosclerosis and restenosis, but key regulators remain unclear. Here, the authors show DDIT4 promotes this switch via pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inhibition, reducing acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation, repressing contractile genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
item.description: The speed of binding color and orientation in an alternating stream is limited by the duration of a recurrent process in visual cortex. Binding is accomplished by a gradual attentional bias of this process, causing a form of stroboscopic stationarity.

item.title: Nature Communications: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
item.description: The authors find that in rats, responses to witnessing others’ distress scale with hippocampal place-field firing, linking observed danger to the observer’s location. Associated spatial maps are stabilized and reactivated, particularly in the intermediate hippocampus.

item.title: Nature Communications: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
item.description: Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
item.description: Here the authors used long-term monitoring of 32 mother-child pairs to report that fetal day-night activity rhythms align with maternal circadian patterns, and that fetal sleep timing associates maternal sleep regularity and post-natal infant sleep patterns. These findings suggest that individual differences in sleep and circadian behavior may emerge before birth, although confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
item.description: Chloroplasts evolved from a cyanobacterial ancestor. Here authors show a cyanobacterial protein export system was transformed into a chloroplast protein import channel by gaining a specific patch to lock a substrate in place to provide the import conduit.

item.title: Nature Communications: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
item.description: Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
item.description: In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
item.description: Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine.

item.title: Nature Communications: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
item.description: Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
item.description: Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ−1
item.description: Casδ−1 is a recently discovered type V CRISPR endonuclease enabling miniature RNA-guided genome editing. In this study, the authors reveal its structural basis and evolutionary insights, advancing understanding of compact CRISPR systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
item.description: VCP/p97 uses Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 to process polyubiquitylated substrates. Here, the authors show how these adapters coordinate ubiquitin-chain engagement and delivery while adapting to conformational changes in the p97 ATPase motor during substrate processing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
item.description: Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
item.description: Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

item.title: Nature Communications: One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training
item.description: Rare gastrointestinal lesions are seldom seen in endoscopy, limiting data for AI and clinician training. Here, authors present EndoRare, a one-shot retraining-free framework that synthesizes diverse lesion images from one reference to improve diagnosis and training.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
item.description: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma severity. Here the authors use mice deficient in intestinal epithelial cell AhR to show that in the absence of AhR, house dust mite-induced allergic airway disease is heightened in the presence of Candida albicans and fucosylation of lung structural cells affects neutrophil adhesion and retention in inflamed lung tissue involving inhibition of the mucus-utilising bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila .

item.title: Nature Communications: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
item.description: The fluoride transport mechanism of the bacterial fluoride channel (Fluc) remains elusive. Here, authors use molecular dynamics paired with Markov state models to reveal distinct mechanisms in each pore and a functional role for the central sodium.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
item.description: Mutualistic interactions are hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship remains limited. This study finds that, across Poa grasses, fungal endophytes are associated with broader niches and faster niche breadth evolution, but reduced diversification rates.

item.title: Nature Communications: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
item.description: HCN channels regulate electrical activity in the heart and brain, but how voltage sensing is coupled to channel opening remains incompletely understood. Here, authors show that the extracellular turret coordinates voltage-sensor and pore-domain movements to enable channel opening.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
item.description: Aptamers are oligonucleotides selected to bind a specific target. The tertiary structure of a DNA aptamer bound to dopamine reveals a compact fold with few canonical features, illustrating diversity in the conformational landscape of DNA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
item.description: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Shen et al. developed KaML-ESMs, sequence-based models that predict pKa values with accuracy rivaling experiment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
item.description: People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

item.title: Nature Communications: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
item.description: Visualizing how drugs reshape GPCR receptors by cryo-EM has been difficult for many conformational states. Here, authors use designed protein fiducials to image elusive GPCR states, revealing details of ligand induced receptor activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
item.description: Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
item.description: The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
item.description: Using human brain organoids, here authors report that GATOR1 loss impairs GABAergic interneurons via MAFB downregulation, independently of mTOR hyperactivation, offering new mechanistic insights into genetic focal epilepsy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
item.description: A study of French Polynesians found hundreds of genetic variants that are common locally but rare worldwide and that alter metabolite levels and gene activity, including variants linked to lipid levels, type 2 diabetes and gout.

item.title: Nature Communications: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
item.description: This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

item.title: Nature Communications: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
item.description: Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Predicting follow-up cognition using estimated structural and functional connectivity networks and artificial intelligence in multiple sclerosis
item.description: Researchers used AI and clinically acquired MRI scans to estimate brain connectivity networks in people with multiple sclerosis, finding these estimates can moderately predict cognitive performance four years later and highlighting key brain circuits involved in cognition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
item.description: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes drive cancer initiation and progression but are thought to be “undruggable”. Here, the authors show that suppressor transfer RNAs can restore p53 from such mutations to induce tumour regression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
item.description: In this study, authors show that serum metabolites measured before symptoms appear can predict which people with chronic Chagas disease will later develop heart damage, offering a way to identify patients at risk years in advance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular prosthetics for CFTR designed for anion selectivity outperform amphotericin B in cystic fibrosis airway epithelia
item.description: Here the authors design amphotericin B (AmB) to better mimic the missing CFTR ion channel in Cystic Fibrosis airway epithelia. These derivatives formed small molecule ion channels with increased permeability to anions and outperformed AmB.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
item.description: A locally optimized framework that integrates multiple published polygenic risk scores substantially improves disease risk prediction over individual scores, providing a practical strategy for enhancing genetic risk assessment across diverse diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
item.description: This study used phylodynamic modelling of EV-D68 outbreak dynamics and found an association between clade B circulation and acute flaccid myelitis. However, this association weakened after COVID-19 emergence despite a resurgence of EV-D68 cases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial
item.description: Cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy develop immune-related adverse events. Here, the authors report the results of a multi-centre prospective phase Ib/II clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) therapy, showing ECP is a safe therapeutic option that could benefit the treatment of ICI-related inflammatory syndromes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.description: Gallstone disease is common, but its genetic basis remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors conduct a trans‑ancestry GWAS identifying 116 risk loci, linking gallstone susceptibility to lipid and liver metabolism pathways and expanding understanding of disease biology across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: Blood p-tau217 is a leading Alzheimer’s test but is also raised in ALS. Here, the authors show that muscle makes its own form of tau which leaks into the blood, and that detecting brain-derived p-tau217 improves the test’s accuracy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
item.description: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

item.title: Nature Communications: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
item.description: Here, the authors show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O-antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae and that this surface-remodeling adaptation enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
item.description: This study shows that tracking tumor DNA in blood can help predict outcomes, monitor treatment response, and reveal resistance in women receiving bireociclib plus fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
item.description: Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
item.description: Restricting branched-chain amino acids is linked to metabolic benefits. Here, the authors show that valine directly binds ATP5F1B in cardiac tissue from hypertensive male rodents, and that low-valine diet stabilizes this protein by reducing LONP1-mediated degradation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
item.description: This study reveals how persistent TFE3 activation triggers the neurodevelopmental disorder TFE3-NDD by disrupting critical cellular functions, including energy production, lysosomal function, and cell-matrix interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
item.description: Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
item.description: Analysis of 1.35 million emergency department visits found that racial and ethnic disparities in triage scores were concentrated in lower-risk visits, where assessment relies more on clinical judgment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
item.description: This trial demonstrates the safety of sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive therapy in severe malaria in African children and identified, using a continual reassessment method design, the optimal dose to investigate in future trials.

item.title: Nature Communications: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
item.description: Genomic-based tests for Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. Here, the authors find that the multi-model transformer-based method HRDPath could be used as a digital biomarker to improve ovarian cancer diagnosis and therapy selection.’

item.title: Nature Communications: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
item.description: ACSS1 mediates maladaptive mitonuclear communication under nutrient stress, impairing metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis. Targeting ACSS1 preserves bone integrity in diabetic and alcoholic mice by sustaining bone formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
item.description: The KARI dataset maps healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease across >6,000 scans from 1,645 adults. Demonstrating its utility, imaging biomarkers scale with clinical severity, providing a resource to accelerate future Alzheimer research.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
item.description: A study of 2,536 MDR Salmonella genomes across China’s food chain forecasts resistance to 2050. Antibiotic use and population growth associate with rising carbapenem and colistin resistance, with food workers an overlooked last-resort ARG reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
item.description: In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte
item.description: The authors find that the live-attenuated cholera vaccine CVD 103-HgR was 87% effective during the 2024 Mayotte outbreak, averting several hundred cases. Live-attenuated vaccines could complement killed vaccines amid global shortages.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
item.description: Using large-scale plasma proteomics, Kim et al. identify proteins altered in ALS and develop a 10-protein model with high classification accuracy, supporting development of a blood-based tool to facilitate earlier ALS diagnosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: This study shows complementary roles of plasma p-tau217 and eMTBRtau243 across Alzheimer’s disease, supporting their use for blood-based assessment of tau pathology, biological staging and prognosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
item.description: Insulin resistance in skeletal muscle contributes to type 2 diabetes (T2D), but its causes remain unclear. We identify the mitochondrial protein Miro1 as a key regulator of muscle insulin sensitivity, providing new insights into T2D development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB
item.description: In a Lesotho cohort treated with a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB, baseline chest radiographic features (cavities, fibrosis, bilateral disease) and high sputum smear grade, individually and in-combination, predicted slower sputum clearance and increased risk for poor outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
item.description: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, the authors found that short-term, low-dose perioperative glucocorticoids may improve cerebrovascular outcomes as an adjunct to flow diverter therapy for unruptured intracranial aneurysms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
item.description: Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
item.description: In cognitively normal individuals, the rate of change in concentrations of plasma ptau217 and Aβ−42/40 over age differs between APOE ε4 carriers and non-carriers. For p-tau217, the effect of APOE ε4 carriership is stronger in males than females.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration
item.description: Here they use spatial transcriptomics to analyze cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells in zebrafish heart and show that adrenomedullin a and ackr3a are critical in cardiac lymphatic vessel development and immune cell clearance during regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study
item.description: Apelin can counteract water retention and may help correct low blood sodium. Here, the authors show in a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial that intravenous apelin does not meaningfully increase urine output in adults with experimentally induced hyponatremia.

item.title: Nature Communications: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries
item.description: This study of over 100,000 pregnancies in four European countries found that both initial and booster COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy were linked to lower risks of infection and related hospital admission.

item.title: Nature Communications: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
item.description: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
item.description: Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking.

item.title: Nature Communications: LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning
item.description: LitGene is an interpretable AI model that learns gene representations from scientific text and Gene Ontology, enabling zero-shot prediction of gene functions and disease links; it reveals ANGPTL6 as a candidate gene in pulmonary fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization
item.description: How epithelial-derived ITLN1 shapes neutrophil immunity in colorectal cancer remains unclear. The authors here show that ITLN1 promotes STAT3/C/EBPδ-associated neutrophil maturation and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, linking bone marrow granulopoiesis to mature-neutrophil spatial organization and anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration
item.description: This study identifies IL-18 as an inflammatory switch that drives macrophage dysfunction and impairs stem cell function, thereby limiting skeletal regeneration and revealing a potential therapeutic target for bone repair.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
item.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction can occur without obesity. Here, the authors show that it is common in Japanese cohorts and find in mice that hypertensive stress alters macrophage signaling, promoting metabolic remodeling and inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
item.description: The identification of clinically relevant driver alterations in prostate cancer remains elusive. Here, integrative analysis of cancer driver genes using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1,001 men identifies four oncotypes, two of which are associated with poor clinical outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
item.description: Aisyah et al. report nationwide use of Indonesia’s integrated ASIK-SATUSEHAT system for 116 million NCD screening visits, showing broad primary-care adoption alongside variation by service, region, age and sex.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
item.description: In this study, Slavov et al. identify MWPyV DNA in 7.7% of pediatric oropharyngeal samples from Brazil, predominantly in young children and at low viral loads. Genomic analyses reveal distinct viral lineages and evidence of recombination, while electron microscopy provides ultrastructural evidence of MWPyV particles in respiratory specimens.

item.title: Nature Communications: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
item.description: Dietary exposure to nanoplastics is an emerging health concern. Here, the authors show that high-fiber diet reduces nanoplastic gastrointestinal retention, alleviates intestinal injury, and limits organ translocation in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
item.description: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multiorgan injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that USP28 deubiquitinates NMMHC IIA to enhance IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling, thereby driving endothelial necroptosis in sepsis in a male mouse model of sepsis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
item.description: The authors develop MRZ, a Mendelian randomization method that models variant-outcome z-scores as a mixture to separate causal effects from pleiotropy, and validate the causal findings in mouse experiments.

item.title: Nature Communications: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
item.description: The mechanisms driving early axonal and synaptic dysfunction in ALS remain unclear. Here, the authors identify compartment-specific RNA changes and identify SLITRK2 as a driver of axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS using an iNMJ-on-a-chip model.

item.title: Nature Communications: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
item.description: Macrophage pyroptosis has been shown to be involved in acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors find that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) is downregulated in AKI and that loss of RNF130 in myeloid cells aggravates renal pathological damage and that RNF130 decreases macrophage pyroptosis through prevention of ubiquitination and inactivation of PDCD4 and that otherwise PDCD4 promotes phosphorylation of NF-kB and STAT3 leading to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and macrophage pyroptosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
item.description: Here, Garcia-Prieto et al use spatial transcriptomics to reveal progressive endothelial, pneumocyte type I and natural killer cell loss, expansion of myeloid and stromal cells, TGF-β-driven fibrosis signaling and alveolar regeneration programs in fatal COVID-19 lung injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: Klebsiella -dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
item.description: Here, the authors identify a relationship between rotavirus vaccine response, colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, and inflammation across a cohort of infants from three different regions (Panama, Peru, and the U.S.A).’

item.title: Nature Communications: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
item.description: Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: Here the authors analyse mobility and COVID-19 data from 122 countries to examine how changes in movement affected virus transmission. They find that mobility data improved estimates of SARS-CoV-2 spread, particularly in Western Europe and North America.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
item.description: In this randomized controlled trial, authors show that sodium zirconium cyclosilicate helped people with heart failure and chronic kidney disease reach recommended doses of key heart failure medicines, while reducing episodes of high blood potassium without added safety concerns.

item.title: Nature Communications: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
item.description: Researchers linked four Fitbit-derived activity measures, from step count to cadence, to over 400 diseases in 29,303 adults, revealing new associations with conditions including chronic pain and autoimmune disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
item.description: Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
item.description: The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
item.description: Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

item.title: Nature Communications: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
item.description: Using single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, researchers showed the four-eyed fish Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of its ventral retina and regional opsin gene tuning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
item.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced myocarditis is a rare side effect of ICI therapy. Here the authors use multi-omics approaches to characterize the immune cells and mediators involved and find monocytes and ISG15 + CD8 + T cells as well as an 8-protein panel to better distinguish ICI-myocarditis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
item.description: In this study authors showcase a rabbit-to-human translational model that predicts anti-tuberculosis drug distribution in patient lesions and effectively discerns Phase 3 regimen outcomes, helping to design more robust strategies for regimen prioritization.
